title: How the rook moves

D0.outcome: Says that a rook slides any distance along a rank or file and cannot jump over pieces.

D1.outcome: When told 'rook', marks every square a rook can move to: it stops in front of its own pieces and may take the first enemy piece in its way.

D2.outcome: In a busy position where the piece is not named, marks every square the piece on a given square can reach.

D3.outcome: Without a board, says whether a rook can reach a far square in one move, and if not in how many, and notices when one blocker is all that stops it.

misconceptions: The rook can jump over pieces.
The rook can land on a square held by its own piece.
The rook cannot capture a piece standing in its way.
conditions: The rook moves along a rank or a file for any number of free squares.
It stops in front of its own piece and may take the first enemy piece on its line, and then stops there.
contrasts: A piece on the line blocks everything behind it: the squares behind it cannot be reached in one move.
Pieces that stand off the rook's rank and file do not change where the rook can go.
